evidence.title: Reported slowdown limits an automatic acceleration inference
evidence.observation: In a randomized trial, 16 experienced developers completed 246 tasks. Allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19% in that setting.
evidence.evidence_standing: Author-reported bounded randomized trial; not independently reproduced by the Commons
evidence.limitations: Familiar mature repositories and then-current tools limit generalization. The result does not establish that AI never accelerates work. The blog and paper describe the same trial, not independent replications.
evidence.open_questions: Which barrier actually changed, for which users and tasks, before applying constraint compression?
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed summary of the cited author or provider account. Source inspection supports traceability; the Commons has not independently replicated or verified the underlying finding.
evidence.dispute_status: Disputes and retractions not systematically checked
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

relationships.explanation: A measured slowdown challenges treating AI use as automatic barrier reduction. It does not refute the conditional definition.
Later research adds temporal and methodological context; preserves the early-2025 result.

These studies used different developer populations, tasks, tools and periods. A completion-time benefit in Peng does not reverse or replicate the METR mature-repository slowdown; retain both settings and their limitations.

source_dependencies.explanation: Author blog and paper abstract report one trial; they are not two independent confirmations.
